Notes
Our client seeks a Senior Payments Administrator to join their team. Role Profile: To effect payments, handle exceptions and queries, administer products and meet stakeholder needs through various channels. To assist the manager in managing workflows and ensuring that work load is managed and distributed across the team and support junior team members in the execution of their duties in order to provide consistently high levels of customer service. Key Responsibilities: Book and process foreign exchange transactions as per the defined policies and procedures. Deliver exceptional levels of service to internal and external customers by intimately understanding their needs and servicing them appropriately to ensure improved client experience. Identify and escalate any suspicious activity to the manager particularly when it could put the bank at the risk of loss or it is in contravention with Anti-Money Laundering/Know Your Customer regulations, to enable the effective and efficient mitigation of risks. Identify areas for improvements and make recommendations to the Operations Management paying focus to processes that cross over functions, to improve the efficiency and quality of the services provided by the Operations team. Manage inward and outward payment queues to support the manager with allocation of work and ensure that all requests are processed efficiently and in adherence to agreed SLAs. Key Skills and Experience: Secondary/High school/A levels. 3 - 4 years experience in Operations. Experience in general banking.
 If you have the required skills please apply online at searchandselect.com quoting reference number: 16461

Our client seeks a Financial Crime Compliance Officer Specialist to join their team. You will support the implementation of the IOM Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) Policies and Standards. Key Responsibilities: Advise on the collection, capturing and maintenance of data to ensure the information is reliable and therefore will effectively guide critical business decisions. The role requires an expert in Compliance with profound knowledge of the full dimensions of the field, but deep expertise in the relevant area of specialisation. Regulatory environment savvy, with the proven ability to influence all levels of employees across multiple countries and business areas to effectively implement compliance frameworks.

This is a hands-on role suited to someone who enjoys bringing structure to fast-moving projects, collaborating across teams and helping turn ideas into well-executed marketing activity. 
No two days will look the same. Priorities shift quickly, projects move at pace, and you’ll be expected to adapt confidently while keeping activity organised and on track. The Operations Manager is responsible for the safe, compliant and efficient management of Manx Petroleum Limited’s operational activities, including terminal operations, fuel supply, logistics and supporting functions. This is a senior leadership role, accountable for the day-to-day running and continuous improvement of bulk fuel operations, aviation fuel supply, and island-wide distribution. The role ensures that all operational activity is conducted in line with regulatory requirements, industry standards, and company policies, while maintaining high levels of safety, quality, and service delivery. The Operations Manager works closely with the Chief Executive, regulatory bodies, and internal teams to deliver operational excellence, manage risk, and support the ongoing development of the business. Essential candidate requirements: Proven experience in operations management within fuel, logistics, industrial, or similarly regulated environments. Strong understanding of health, safety, and environmental compliance requirements. Experience managing complex operational processes and multi-site activities. Demonstrated leadership experience with the ability to manage and motivate teams. Strong organisational, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Personal characteristics include: Strong leadership presence with a calm and decisive approach. Highly organised and detail-oriented with a focus on safety and compliance. Proactive and resilient, with the ability to manage operational challenges effectively. Excellent communicator with strong stakeholder management skills. Hands-on, practical, and solutions-focused.  Desirable skills, experience and attributes: Experience in petroleum, energy, or aviation fuel operations. Knowledge of regulatory frameworks relating to fuel storage and distribution. Experience working with regulatory authorities. A full role profile is available upon request. To apply please forward your up-to-date CV and a covering letter to Richard Gelder, Chief Executive at RichardG@mp.im

Notes
Are you an experienced and dynamic leader looking to make a real impact in primary care? Peel Group Practice is seeking a highly motivated Practice Manager to lead our dedicated team and help drive the future of our well-established and forward-thinking GP practice.
About Us:
Peel Group Practice is a friendly, patient-focused NHS GP surgery providing high-quality care to our local community. With a strong commitment to clinical excellence, staff wellbeing, and continuous improvement, we pride ourselves on being a supportive and innovative place to work.
We are a three partner practice serving 9250 patients, with a skilled multidisciplinary team including GPs, Nurses,  HCAs, Pharmacy Technician, and administrative staff. We work closely with our Manx Care and wider health system partners to deliver outstanding care.
Role Summary:
As Practice Manager, you will lead the operational management of the Practice and ensure smooth day-to-day functioning. You’ll be responsible for strategic planning, HR, finance, patient services, compliance, and implementing changes in line with Manx Care policy and local needs.
Key responsibilities:
Provide strategic leadership and effective management across all areas of the Practice.
Oversee HR and staffing, including recruitment, training, and performance management – with the assistance of the practice support officer.
Manage Practice finances, budgets, and reporting.
Ensure compliance with local CQC, Health & Safety, GDPR, and other regulatory frameworks.
Optimise use of clinical systems and digital tools.
Drive continuous improvement in service delivery, patient experience, and staff wellbeing.
Opportunity to work in a progressive, stable, and well-organised environment.
What We’re Looking For:
Proven leadership and management experience (ideally in Primary Care or healthcare).
Strong business and financial acumen.
Excellent interpersonal and organisational skills.
Working knowledge of NHS structures and policies (desirable).
A proactive and collaborative approach to problem-solving and innovation.
We Offer:
Competitive salary (negotiable).
Pension.
Death in service. 
Annual leave and sick pay.
Supportive, forward-thinking team.
A DBS check will be required – paid for by the Practice.
How to Apply:
Please submit your CV and a covering letter outlining your suitability for the role to:
peelmgt@gov.im or Peel Group Practice, Management Team, Albany Road, Peel, IM5 1HU.
For informal enquiries, contact 693890 Closing date: 5th June 2026.

Job Description
To lead the Credit Risk function for the Business and Commercial Banking business unit (BU) in country, ensuring effective credit risk management across the entire credit lifecycle. To implement the BU's credit strategy in alignment with country-level credit objectives, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements, while supporting sustainable business growth and maintaining a high-quality credit portfolio.

Qualifications:
First Degree in Business Commerce, Finance and Accounting, Generic Management or Risk Management.
Postgraduate in Degree in Business Commerce, Finance and Accounting, Generic Management or Risk Management (Advantageous).

Experience:
This role requires a seasoned leader and expert in Risk management with extensive knowledge of the entire credit lifecycle, together with comprehensive experience within Real Estate Finance and the property sector, including but not limited to, structuring, assessing and managing credit exposures related to property transactions and development projects.
Proven ability to manage stressed and distressed clients, with a track record of implementing effective risk mitigation strategies, negotiating restructuring solutions, and safeguarding the bank’s interests, while maintaining client relationships.
Minimum 5 years People Leadership experience at a Senior organisational level, with a focus on talent management, resourcing, development and retention.
Regulatory environment savvy, a proven track record in large scale and high-level leadership and proactively develop and manage relationships with key internal and external stakeholders and external legal counsel, relevant to the business strategy. Ability to build and develop relationships across the bank with various stakeholders, with the intention of breaking down silos to maximise business growth.
8-10 years’ Experience in managing credit origination (both intuitive and automated) and credit operations, with an ability to handle all aspects of client engagement, including coordinating and execution of transactions.

Behavioural Competencies:
Developing Expertise.   
Challenging Ideas.         
Convincing People. 
Developing Strategies.
Directing People.
Building Relationships.

Technical Competencies:
Economic Capital Management.           
Evaluating Risk Management Effectiveness.     
Risk Acceptance, Awareness, Identification and Management.      
Debt Capacity modelling proficiency.
PD/LGD/EAD understanding and application.
Collateral valuation, legal perfection and Security package design.
Intercreditor & priority structures.
Covenant architecture.
Counterparty credibility assessment, including Pre-sale, Lease & tenant analysis.

Notes
Key Responsibilities:
Develop the overall promotional strategy across Sportsbook and Gaming products, aligned with business KPIs and customer behaviour.
Own the promotional calendars, ensuring coverage of key sporting events, gaming seasonality, and commercial objectives.
Identify opportunities to introduce new, compelling promotional formats and offers that differentiate our brands in their respective markets.
Design and manage a wide range of promotional mechanics such as Bet & Gets, Deposit Offers, Cashback, Missions, Tournaments, Price Boosts, cross-product offers.
Work with Product and Tech teams to improve promotional tools, automation, and customer experience.
Oversee end-to-end campaign delivery: briefing, setup, QA, launch, monitoring, and post-campaign review.
Monitor campaign performance and make real-time optimisations based on data, trading impact, and customer response.
Ensure promotions are commercially efficient, clearly communicated, and fully compliant with responsible gambling and regulatory standards.
Track key metrics including participation, incremental revenue, retention uplift, and bonus efficiency.
Partner with BI and Data teams to analyse promotional results and identify actionable insights.
Produce clear, practical reporting to inform future campaign planning and improvements.
Work closely with Sportsbook, Casino, CRM, Trading, Product, Compliance, and Customer Support teams to ensure smooth execution.
Support CRM and Lifecycle teams to integrate promotions into customer journeys and segmentation strategies.
Collaborate with Trading to balance customer appeal with sustainable risk management.
Team Contribution:
Mentor junior team members and help upskill the wider commercial teams on promotional strategy and mechanics.
Manage external suppliers and vendors involved in promotional tooling or gamification solutions.
Provide input into product roadmaps, commercial forecasts, and budget planning.
Requirements:
5+ years of experience in online gaming or sportsbook promotions,CRM, or product marketing.
Commercially minded, with a good balance of creativity and analytical thinking.
Strong understanding of Sportsbook mechanics, betting behaviour, and gaming product ecosystems.
Proven track record in designing, delivering, and optimising high- impact promotional campaigns.
Excellent analytical skills with proficiency in tools like Excel, PowerBI, or similar.
Experience working with promotional tools, campaign management systems, and bonus engines.
Organised, detail-focused, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, live environment.
Confident communicator who can work effectively with a range of stakeholders.

Additional related, duties may be assigned by the Line Manager in line with business.

For more details and to apply contact talent@silverspin.com

Our client seeks a Management Accountant to join their Finance Team. Role Profile: You In this role, you'll play a key part in supporting the financial health and strategic direction of the Group. You'll contribute to the delivery of accurate, insightful financial reporting and analysis, helping to inform decision-making and drive performance across the Group. Joining the bank and its mission to provide financial excellence by monitoring performance, managing costs, assessing risks, and delivering strategic insights that drive informed decision-making. You'll report to the Head of Management Accounting and the Group Financial Controller, supporting the Finance Director and wider Finance Team in delivering accurate financial reporting and analysis across the Group. Key Responsibilities: Prepare accurate and timely monthly management accounts the bank and its subsidiaries. Support financial reporting with journal entries, reconciliations, VAT and tax filings, and management pack preparation. Drive continuous improvement in reporting through KPIs, variance analysis, and trend insights. Collaborate with teams across the business, respond to financial queries, and support team development. Provide cover for senior finance roles and ensure compliance with internal policies and regulatory requirements. Key Skills and Experience: A recognised accountant qualification, be part-qualified, or have relevant industry experience. Knowledge of IFRS, UK Accounting Standards, and ERP systems (preferably SUN and Xero). Working knowledge of relational database theory sufficient to perform database queries. Excellent Excel and numeracy skills. Strong organisation and communication skills. Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines. All applications will be treated with the utmost discretion.
 If you have the required skills please apply online at searchandselect.com quoting reference number: 16434

Are you a skilled Vehicle Technician looking to take the next step in your career? We are Nissan's authorised service & repair workshop on the Isle of Man, and we are looking for a talented, motivated, and customer-focused individual to join our dynamic workshop team in Ballasalla.
This is a fantastic opportunity to work with one of the world's leading automotive brands, utilising the latest diagnostic equipment and manufacturer training. Whether you are working on routine servicing or complex diagnostics and repairs, you will play a vital role in keeping our customers safely on the road.

In this role, you will be responsible for carrying out servicing, maintenance, and repairs on Nissan vehicles to the highest manufacturer standards. A core part of the position involves performing diagnostic work using Nissan's specialist CONSULT diagnostic equipment, completing warranty repairs, and supporting technical service campaigns. You will conduct thorough vehicle health checks and communicate your findings clearly to our service advisors, while proactively identifying any faults or emerging issues during inspection. You will also be expected to maintain a clean, safe, and well-organised workshop environment at all times, complete job cards and workshop documentation accurately, and keep your technical knowledge current through Nissan's ongoing manufacturer training programmes.

We are seeking a candidate who holds a recognised automotive qualification such as NVQ Level 2 or 3, City & Guilds, or an equivalent accreditation, along with proven hands-on experience as a Vehicle Technician in either a franchised or independent workshop setting. You should have solid experience working with modern vehicle diagnostic systems, and whilst Nissan or other manufacturer-brand training is desirable, it is by no means essential as full training will be provided. Above all, we are looking for someone who takes pride in the quality of their work, communicates well with colleagues and customers alike, holds a full valid Isle of Man driving licence, and has the drive and initiative to perform equally well working independently or as part of a close-knit team.

To apply for this position, please send your CV and a covering letter to: gm@athol.co.im

Notes
Onchan District Commissioners are seeking a motivated and customer focussed Library Assistant to support the day-to-day running of our busy and welcoming public library.  This is a varied and rewarding role, providing a high-quality essential service to the community and supporting the Head librarian in delivering a high-quality library experience.  This is an opportunity to play a key role in a valued community service, helping people access information, develop skills and most importantly, enjoy reading.  In this role you will take responsibility for opening, running and closing the library in the absence of the Head Librarian.  You will provide a proactive and friendly service to all customers ensuring the library remains an accessible, organised and engaging space for the community.  We are looking for someone who is committed to providing excellent customer service, has good verbal communication and interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively with all sections of the community.   Applicants should have a keen interest in books, public access to information and supporting local communities. Candidates should possess a minimum of five GSCEs Grade C or above including English and Mathematics (or equivalent), be computer literate and competent in using Microsoft Office programmes, or similar packages with the ability to adapt to new systems.  Excellent written communication skills are required along with a conscientious and methodical approach to work.  Further information about the services offered can be found on the Library Website: www.onchan.org.im/library.        A copy of the job description and details about how to apply can be found at: https://jobs.exceedoutsourcing.co.uk/jobs/Onchan-District-Commissioners/20081000008703002/Library-Assistant?source=CareerSite

IFGL is seeking a highly organised and detail-oriented Due Diligence Specialist & Legal Support professional to join our Risk, Legal & Compliance team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with experience in corporate due diligence, legal administration, or company secretarial support who is looking to develop their career within a professional financial services environment.

Reporting to the Data Protection Officer & Legal Specialist, you will be responsible for maintaining accurate and up-to-date corporate due diligence records for IFGL legal entities. You will work closely with relationship owners across the business to manage and review third-party due diligence requests and ensure appropriate documentation is supplied consistently and accurately.

You will also provide broader legal and governance support, including assistance with board resolutions, governance committee administration, and minute taking.

The main duties for the role holder will include:
Maintain current and accurate records of corporate due diligence documentation. 
Review, approve, and record non-standard due diligence responses. 
Respond to internal and external due diligence queries in a timely manner. 
Conduct regular reviews of due diligence records to ensure accuracy and compliance. 
Support internal stakeholders with guidance on due diligence requirements and documentation standards. 
Assist the wider Group Legal Team with data protection and corporate governance activities. 
Prepare board resolutions and provide minute-taking support for governance committees. 

To ensure that this role is carried out to the desired level, the successful candidates will need to demonstrate the following skills and experience:
Good understanding of corporate legal structures. 
Excellent attention to detail and ability to work accurately under pressure. 
Strong organisational and planning skills. 
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision. 
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
Ideally has minimum of two years’ experience within a company secretarial, legal support, or financial services environment.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
If you are interested in applying for this position, please forward your current CV with a covering letter to careers@ifg-ltd.com   
We encourage and welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds because we embrace diversity and inclusivity within our business.
The closing date for this vacancy will be 5 June 2026.

Notes
Altenar is a leading IT company founded in 2011 and headquartered in the Isle of Man, with offices in Malta, Greece, Georgia, Brazil and Uruguay.
We are seeking a proactive and detail oriented Junior Legal/Contracts Officer to support the legal, contracts, and governance functions of the business.
Key Responsibilities:
Assisting with the corporate governance of the Altenar group of Companies, including arranging board meetings and preparing agendas and board packs.
Assisting with the creation and preparation of documents for presentation to the Board of Directors for review and signature, particularly customer onboarding documentation.
Attending board meetings to assist with the recording and preparation of accurate board minutes.
Working with the Contracts Manager to ensure legal documents progress efficiently from drafting and collaboration (with all relevant stakeholders) through negotiation to  execution.
Ensuring physical and electronic filing is completed promptly and accurately, including  maintaining internal document databases and records.
Assisting the Compliance department with customer and supplier on-boarding processes.
Supporting general company administration, including insurance and data protection renewals and other corporate administrative requirements as they  arise. 
Assisting with banking administration and payment processes, as required.
Providing general administrative and ad-hoc business support as required from time to time.

Essential Requirements:
Good standard of general education, including GCSEs (or equivalent) in English and Maths.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and competing priorities.
Strong written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and professionalism.
Proactive and self motivated approach, with the ability to work independently and take ownership of tasks.
Willingness and aptitude to learn new processes, systems, and areas of the business.
Ability to follow instruction carefully while also using initiative and sound judgement

Desirable Requirements:
Previous experience in an administrative, governance, legal support, compliance or company secretarial role, including exposure to board meetings or governance processes
Experience working within a regulated industry or professional services environment.
Familiarity with legal documentation, contracts administration, or compliance processes.
Experience maintaining document management systems or internal databases.
Understanding of customer and supplier onboarding processes.
Knowledge of data protection requirements and general corporate administration.

For more details and to apply contact job@altenar.com

Oversee the preparation of statistics, dashboards and information for both internal stakeholders and Regulators. Submit reports and Management Information to the line manager for use by the relevant steering committee. Key Skills and Experience: Diploma in Risk Management (Required). The Interim Governance and Corporate Services Officer will provide high-level administrative, governance and executive support to the Chief Executive/Clerk of a local Commissioners during a period of sickness cover. The role is intended to ensure continuity of corporate governance, policy development and senior administrative functions, and requires someone capable of operating with a high degree of autonomy and discretion.

The postholder will support the Chief Executive/Clerk in fulfilling statutory and corporate governance responsibilities, including the preparation and review of policies, procedures and governance documentation. They will assist in the coordination of committee and board processes, which will include preparing agendas, managing documentation and ensuring that actions are recorded and followed through appropriately. The role also involves overseeing complex administrative activity across the organisation and ensuring that internal processes are maintained to a high standard.

In addition, the Interim Governance and Corporate Services Officer may provide line management support and assist in coordinating staff activities where required. The role will also involve working with financial and budgetary information and supporting basic accountancy-related processes where necessary, although formal accountancy experience is desirable rather than essential.

The postholder will be expected to ensure compliance with relevant legislation, internal policies and recognised standards of good governance within a local authority context. They will act as a key point of contact for internal teams and external stakeholders in relation to governance and corporate services matters, and will be expected to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion at all times.

The ideal candidate will have experience in corporate governance, senior administrative roles or executive support functions, along with experience in drafting formal policies, reports and governance documents. Strong organisational and communication skills are essential, as is the ability to manage competing priorities and work independently. Experience of line management and familiarity with local government or public sector environments would be advantageous.

Notes
The Interim Governance and Corporate Services Officer will provide high-level administrative, governance and executive support to the Chief Executive/Clerk of a local Commissioners during a period of sickness cover. The role is intended to ensure continuity of corporate governance, policy development and senior administrative functions, and requires someone capable of operating with a high degree of autonomy and discretion.

The postholder will support the Chief Executive/Clerk in fulfilling statutory and corporate governance responsibilities, including the preparation and review of policies, procedures and governance documentation. They will assist in the coordination of committee and board processes, which will include preparing agendas, managing documentation and ensuring that actions are recorded and followed through appropriately. The role also involves overseeing complex administrative activity across the organisation and ensuring that internal processes are maintained to a high standard.

In addition, the Interim Governance and Corporate Services Officer may provide line management support and assist in coordinating staff activities where required. The role will also involve working with financial and budgetary information and supporting basic accountancy-related processes where necessary, although formal accountancy experience is desirable rather than essential.

The postholder will be expected to ensure compliance with relevant legislation, internal policies and recognised standards of good governance within a local authority context. They will act as a key point of contact for internal teams and external stakeholders in relation to governance and corporate services matters, and will be expected to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion at all times.

The ideal candidate will have experience in corporate governance, senior administrative roles or executive support functions, along with experience in drafting formal policies, reports and governance documents. Strong organisational and communication skills are essential, as is the ability to manage competing priorities and work independently. Experience of line management and familiarity with local government or public sector environments would be advantageous.

For more information and to apply please e-mail luke@recruitmentworks.im

Notes
Our client seeks a Compliance Officer to join their team. Role Profile: To support the implementation of the Compliance Monitoring Programme ('CMP'), thereby ensuring the business is protected against financial crime, regulatory, reputational and operational risk. To assist the Compliance Team with fulfilment of all Compliance and regulatory responsibilities. To ensure the CMP is maintained and updated as necessary in line with changes to any regulatory requirement. Key Responsibilities: To support the implementation of the CMP, ensuring no backlogs develop. To ensure that findings are accurately logged and monitored to a satisfactory conclusion. Based on findings, suggest actions required e.g. additional training, increased / reduced frequency of specific tests, system enhancements where appropriate. To assist with provision of MI for Board reporting. To record and escalate significant findings to the Head of ComplianceTo assist in managing and supporting departmental workload and critical tasks, such as Compliance Regulatory returns and compliance registers. To ensure testing criteria remains consistent with updated systems and controls and remains effectiveWorking with the business to strengthen its compliance culture by being approachable and clearly articulating requirements. To provide demonstrable support for the strategy of the Isle of Man business and the wider Group. Key Skills and Experience: The post-holder must have appropriate professional compliance qualifications or significant experience in a compliance role. Prior experience in developing and delivering a Compliance Monitoring Plan (CMP). Strong knowledge of the Isle of Man regulatory framework and international compliance standards. Experience within the TCSP sector (preferred but not essential). Ability to adapt to regulatory changes and implement best practices effectively. Strong report writing skills. Personal Attribute: Excellent organisational skills; Great inter-personal skills to communicate CMP Findings with the business lines and confidently discuss the way in which issues can be resolved; Ability to build and develop strong working relationships at all levels; High level of self-motivation and discipline.
 If you have the required skills please apply online at searchandselect.com quoting reference number: 16542

Notes
Join the Isle of Man’s longest-established independent investment firm.
Established in 1946, Ramsey Crookall is the island’s most experienced and trusted firm of stockbrokers and investment managers. We’re a business that has built a reputation for professionalism, integrity, and exceptional client service. We continue to evolve, combining traditional values with modern technology to meet the needs and expectations of our clients.

The Role:
We’re looking for an organised and motivated Administrator to join our Corporate Actions team. In this role, you’ll be responsible for supporting the end-to-end processing of corporate actions events and ensuring the timely and accurate settlement of transactions.
You’ll work closely with colleagues across the business as well as custodians, brokers, and other external partners to ensure corporate events are managed effectively and client outcomes are delivered to a high standard.
This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working with detail, managing deadlines, and developing specialist knowledge within corporate actions. Previous experience in this area would be highly beneficial, though training and support will be provided.

Key Responsibilities:
Process a wide range of corporate actions, including dividends, interest payments, rights issues, mergers, and stock splits.
Monitor and reconcile entitlements, ensuring accuracy and timely processing.
Manage client elections and ensure instructions are submitted within required deadlines.
Liaise with custodians, brokers, and internal teams to obtain and validate corporate action information.
Support the settlements function, ensuring trades are settled efficiently and exceptions are resolved promptly.
Investigate and resolve discrepancies related to asset servicing and settlements.
Maintain accurate records and update internal systems accordingly.
Assist in improving processes to enhance efficiency and reduce operational risk.

About You:
Strong attention to detail and accuracy in your work.
Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines.
Confident communicator – clear, professional, and proactive.
Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
Problem-solving mindset with a proactive approach to resolving issues.
Previous experience in corporate actions, settlements, or asset servicing is highly desirable.

Benefits:
Competitive salary and performance-based bonuses.
Comprehensive health benefits package.
Non-contributory pension plan.
Professional development opportunities.
Free parking.

Why Join Us?
At Ramsey Crookall, you’ll be part of a friendly and professional team that values expertise, collaboration, and integrity. We offer a supportive environment where accuracy and service are key, and where your contribution directly supports our clients’ success.

For more details and to apply contact hr@ramseycrookall.com

We are looking for an experienced, values?driven Service Manager to lead our Family Support and Supervised Contact services. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who wants to combine strong operational leadership with the freedom to think creatively, test new ideas, and shape how services grow and improve. You will oversee two closely connected services, supporting teams to deliver safe, high?quality, child?centred practice, while also creating the conditions for staff to thrive.

We’re looking for a Service Manager who believes great outcomes for families start with healthy teams, trust and creativity. In our service, great ideas don’t need permission! You will be trusted, supported and empowered to lead with innovative approaches.

You’ll lead our Family Support and Supervised Contact services in an organisation known for its positive culture, flexible working and flat structure – where people are encouraged to think differently, test new ideas and speak up.

Main Responsibilities:
Leading and developing two services to deliver safe, effective and compassionate support to children and families.
Creating a team culture where staff feel confident, supported and empowered.
Supporting innovation and continuous improvement, helping new ideas to flourish into practice. 
Working collaboratively with commissioners, partners and senior colleagues.
Ensuring strong governance, safeguarding, quality assurance and performance oversight.
Balancing operational delivery with strategic thinking and service development.

Main Requirements (for details check the job description and person specification):
Experience of managing services within family support, supervised contact, safeguarding or related fields.
A leadership style that is relational, inclusive and strengths?based.
Confidence to work autonomously, while valuing collaboration and shared decision?making.
Curiosity, creativity and the courage to think beyond ‘how things have always been done’.
A commitment to reflective practice, learning and continuous improvement.
We are particularly keen to hear from people who are excited by the idea of shaping services.

To Apply:
Visit our website using the below link and fill out our digital application form

Notes
Our client, a long established fiduciary services business, is seeking a senior individual to take responsibility for its client administration function. The role sits at senior level within the organisation and combines operational oversight, team coordination and direct involvement in complex fiduciary client matters. The focus is on maintaining high service standards, ensuring regulatory obligations are met and supporting the effective running of the function. Key Responsibilities: Oversee day-to-day fiduciary administration activity, ensuring workloads are prioritised and deadlines consistently achieved. Take responsibility for a small portfolio of trust and company structures, including more complex or sensitive arrangements. Act as escalation point for technical fiduciary matters requiring experience and sound judgement. Maintain oversight of client review cycles, periodic compliance activity and associated deadlines. Monitor debtor balances and broader operational risk indicators, ensuring appropriate follow-up and resolution. Review and interpret management information relating to workload, performance and client activity. Support senior stakeholders with operational planning and client-related matters as required. Contribute to the refinement of internal processes, controls and procedural consistency. Provide day-to-day structure across a small administration team, supporting clarity of expectations and delivery standards. Assist with development of team capability through feedback, guidance and on the job support. Maintain effective working relationships with clients, intermediaries and other stakeholders. Key Skills and Experience: Significant experience in fiduciary administration within trust and company services. Strong technical understanding of trust and corporate structures and relevant regulatory frameworks. Previous experience in a supervisory, senior leadership position. Comfortable managing complex fiduciary matters and working under regulatory scrutiny. Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities in a structured way. Clear, practical communicator with a professional and commercially aware approach. Additional Requirements: STEP, CGI/ICSA or equivalent professional qualification would be beneficial but is not essential. Solid experience working within Isle of Man fiduciary regulatory and governance environments. Confident user of standard administration and reporting systems. 
 If you have the required skills please apply online at searchandselect.com quoting reference number: 16520

Our client seeks an experienced Business Analyst to join their Change Department for a 6-month contract. The successful candidate will define business requirements, ways of working and governance needed to ensure Microsoft 365 (including Copilot and SharePoint Online) deliver measurable value across the Company. Key Responsibilities: Define standardised business requirements and ways of working across Microsoft 365 applications, including (but not limited to): Teams, SharePoint, Planner, Loop, Forms, Bookings, Project, Viva Engage. Work with business champions to define business-led requirements for information ownership and accountability (with a strong focus on SharePoint Online) as well as community and collaboration ownership models. Define business-led requirements for data quality and information structure, feeding into project requirements. Identify business and organisational requirements needed to safely enable Copilot. Provide clear, structured inputs into governance and policy design for M365 applications. Define measurable benefits, outcomes, and success criteria for M365 and Copilot adoption. Work closely with 3rd party suppliers to drive timely delivery. Contribute to training content and collaborate closely with the M365 Trainer. Manage and build the project backlog, ensuring clear and actionable requirements. Provide BA input into: Scope definition (in/out), risks, assumptions, and dependencies and options analysis for M365 enablement. Key Skills & Experience: Proven experience as a Business Analyst within digital transformation or enterprise tooling programmes. Strong understanding of Microsoft 365 applications and their business use cases. Experience in defining business processes, governance, operating models and requirements. Excellent stakeholder engagement skills, including working with business champions and senior leaders. Ability to translate business needs into structured, clear documentation and backlogs. Strong understanding of information management concepts (ownership, structure, data quality). Experience working with suppliers and internal delivery teams in a project environment. Ideally have exposure to Microsoft Copilot or similar AI?enabled business tools.Experience with Azure Cloud or DevOps would be desirable. 
 If you have the required skills please apply online at searchandselect.com quoting reference number: 16346

Notes
Head of Compliance – AstroPay Global (IOM) Limited.
The role in a nutshell: Senior compliance leader for the Isle of Man entity, holding the R13 Controlled Function. Reports directly to the Board and Group CCO, operating with significant independence.

What matters most:
Core responsibilities:

R13 Controlled Function holder before the local regulator (IOMFSA).
Own the full compliance framework under the Class 8 licence (payments/e-money).
Supervise the MLRO and lead the IOM compliance team.
Primary point of contact with the IOMFSA.
Build and maintain policies, procedures, and the Compliance Monitoring Program.
Board-level reporting and regulatory submissions.

Required profile:

5+ years in financial services compliance, in a senior role.
Deep knowledge of Isle of Man regulatory framework (FSA 2008, Rule Book 2016, AML/CFT).
Hands-on experience dealing directly with regulators.
Relevant professional qualification (e.g. ICA Diploma).
FinTech, payments, or e-money background highly desirable.

First 6 months focus:

Audit the existing compliance framework, identify gaps, and build an improvement roadmap.
Establish strong relationships with IOMFSA, the Board, and key internal stakeholders.

Nice to haves:

Multi-jurisdiction compliance experience.
Compliance tech / data analytics exposure.
Spanish language skills.

Our client is seeking a Safety & Compliance Officer to provide crucial day-to-day support to the Safety and Compliance Department. This role will involve monitoring crew and vessel certification, ensuring regulatory compliance, and facilitating effective communications. The successful candidate will also play an active role in the development and maintenance of the award-winning electronic Safety Management System (eSMS), working closely with Yacht Managers and participating in the Emergency Response Team. Responsibilities include maintaining up-to-date lists of current crew and statutory certificates for the yachts, liaising with clients and crew to facilitate the renewal of necessary certifications, and assisting the Crewing and Recruitment Departments with crew-related queries. Additionally, the candidate will assist with onboard safety and security management for clients and review safety and security reports as needed. Reporting directly to the Safety and Compliance Manager, the ideal candidate will be highly motivated to provide exceptional service to clients and crew, demonstrating strong knowledge of maritime regulations and certification processes. Please email team@itchyfeet.im or follow the below link for further information and for details on how to apply https://itchyfeetoffshore.com/jobs/36280-safety-compliance-officer-isle-of-man/

Notes
About Us:

We are one of the Isle of Man’s leading automotive dealerships delivering an outstanding ownership experience to our customers across the island. Our team is built on trust, professionalism, and a genuine passion for all things automotive, and we are now looking to expand that team with the addition of a talented and driven Car Salesperson.

The Role:

This is an exciting opportunity for an ambitious individual to join our busy sales floor and become a key part of our customer-facing team. As a Car Salesperson, you will be responsible for guiding customers through every stage of their vehicle purchase, from the initial enquiry and showroom visit right through to handover and beyond. You will develop lasting relationships with both new and returning customers, ensuring that every interaction reflects the high standards our dealership is known for.
Day to day, you will be meeting and greeting customers, understanding their needs, presenting and demonstrating the vehicles, preparing finance proposals, and negotiating sales in a professional and transparent manner. You will also be expected to manage your own customer pipeline, follow up on leads, and work towards individual and team sales targets. Full product training will be provided, so while knowledge of vehicles is an advantage, it is certainly not essential.

What We’re Looking For:

We are looking for someone with a natural flair for sales and a genuine enthusiasm for engaging with people. Previous experience in automotive retail is desirable, but we welcome applications from candidates who have a strong background in any customer-facing or target-driven sales environment. What matters most to us is attitude, energy, and a commitment to delivering an exceptional experience every time.
You will need to be an excellent communicator who can build rapport quickly, listen carefully to what customers want, and present solutions with confidence and clarity. Good organisational skills and the ability to manage your time effectively are also important, as is a proactive approach to generating and following up on sales opportunities. A full, clean driving licence is essential for this role.

What We Offer:

In return for your hard work and dedication, we offer a competitive basic salary alongside an attractive commission structure that rewards your results. You will receive ongoing training, giving you industry-recognised qualifications and keeping your product knowledge sharp. We provide a supportive and friendly working environment where your development is taken seriously.

This is a fantastic chance to build a rewarding long-term career with an established and respected dealership, in a role where your effort genuinely makes a difference. The Isle of Man is a great place to live and work, and we are proud to be part of its community.

How to Apply:

If you have the drive and personality to excel in this role, we would love to hear from you. Please send your CV and a brief covering letter to gm@athol.co.im

As an Assistant Manager you will support your Store Leader to deliver excellent customer care and operational standards every day by connecting with customers to gain a deep understanding of their needs. 
Working across both retail and pharmacy, you will lead and inspire your team by demonstrating your leadership skills on the shop floor, showcasing how to provide brilliant service and care.

Key responsibilities include leading your team to deliver business growth by providing excellent care to customers and patients, while taking responsibility for the performance and development of your team through regular coaching and reviews. It would also be beneficial to have experience working within community pharmacy and confidence in navigating and embracing new technology.

Notes
The postholder will contribute to existing research and survey programmes focussed on the extensive network of Manx Marine Nature Reserves (https://www.gov.im/MNR). This network includes Port Erin Bay MNR which has been closed to mobile gear fishing since 1989 and Ramsey Bay MNR which features a designated Fisheries Management Zone. A primary focus of the role will be to support the establishment of a continuous marine benthic monitoring programme, both inside the MNRs and in the wider territorial sea as required, employing a range of methods which may include video mapping and benthic sampling. The post-holder will contribute to the generation of georeferenced habitat maps and species distribution data as well as investigating the distribution and ecology of key habitats including seagrass, maerl, Modiolus reefs and offshore mud. The role will also involve providing data and evidence-based advice for the development of MNR management plans and on the impacts of marine developments (e.g. wind farms) to support effective and sustainable marine conservation management. Where appropriate there may be an opportunity for the post-holder to register for a PhD to be undertaken alongside the responsibilities of the role.The successful candidate will have a degree in the field of marine science or related area OR equivalent experience, and a desire to be part of a successful team delivering world class science research and advice to enable sustainable management of coastal seas.
The successful candidate will have a degree in the field of marine science or related area OR equivalent experience, and a desire to be part of a successful team delivering world class science research and advice to enable sustainable management of coastal seas. Successful candidates must be capable of passing an ENG1 sea-going medical and Sea Survival course, be physically fit and able to work at sea on a variety of vessels including during potentially less favourable sea conditions. A current clean, valid driving licence is required.

The postholder will be based full-time in the Isle of Man at the Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture (DEFA). Applications will only be accepted via our on-line recruitment website, jobs.bangor.ac.uk. However, in cases of access issues due to disability, paper application forms are available by telephoning 01248 383865. The closing date for applications is 5th June 2026 . Shortlisted candidates must be available for interview at the end of June. Informal enquiries can be made to Prof. Stuart Jenkins 00 44 (0) 1248 382896 or s.jenkins@bangor.ac.uk

Notes
MAIN PURPOSE OF JOB: 
Stock management, Customs, Purchasing, receiving all raw materials at Albion, weighing/counting and recording accurately in an easy to follow stock location system. Issuing trims and yarn to workshops for production and returning unused materials to stock once production is completed. Responsible for arranging import and export of goods as required and ensuring smooth customs clearance for imports when necessary. 
DUTIES INCLUDE: 
To purchase raw materials, packaging materials required for production, packing and shipping, such as pallets, boxes, and other supplies.
Assist in the yarn calculation and raising the yarn purchase order with the yarn supplier.
Assist in the raising of the Trims purchase order.
Ensure that the yarn is received accurately and with proper checks.
Ensure that the yarn is recorded properly in the ERP system.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date stock levels and locations within the company system.
Store all yarn correctly in accordance with Albion’s stock control procedures, ensuring the stockroom is kept clean, tidy, and well organized.
Ensure all system records are kept updated in a timely and accurate manner.
Distribute trims to the relevant workshops for production, maintaining clear and traceable records of what was issued and when.
Liaise with freight forwarding and shipping companies to ensure all paperwork is completed accurately for smooth customs clearance of inbound and outbound goods.
Arrange transportation for bulk shipments to clients when necessary.
Assist with dispatching packed goods, ensuring all packing is completed correctly and on schedule.
Maintain cleanliness and adhere to all safety procedures within the warehouse.
Handle the Customs special procedures like IPR and OPR and filing the quarterly returns.

REQUIRMENTS:

Accuracy and attention to detail.
Strong organisational skills.  
Ability to multitask and prioritise effectively in a fast paced environment.
Experience in a previous logistics role desirable, with knowledge of new EU import/export requirements will be preferable.

For more details and to apply contact rippal@albionknit.com
